PART_1_INTRODUCTION.title: Introduction
PART_1_INTRODUCTION.fundamental_principle: The entire language or speech is nothing but the sequence of vowels and consonants

linguistic_sequences.devanagari: व्यञ्जनम् + व्यञ्जनम् + व्यञ्जनम् स्वरः and so on

key_facts: There will not be any ending or limitation to this sequence
Native speakers give meaningful pauses to sequence flow, Sometimes.
Sometimes, they Continuously speak without any break, especially when they speack fast
However, local speakers understand this clearly. But others face many problems.
At the sametime, language gets changed in order to place and time.
Rishis understood the information that is coded in the form for squence of vowels and consonants.
So they artificially created धातुs, प्रातिपदिकs, उपसर्गs, etc. to break sequences logically
Sometimes, it is only imagination, those forms not used in the society. Ex: लट्, लिट् etc.
With the hlep of this imagination, we can understand the intention and information of the speaker accurately.
After breaking down the sequences of vowels and consonants, it becomes a problem for laymen to understand where and how to join
With help of imagination, we can break the sequences of vowels and consonants meaningfully.
So, to learn the rules of breaking the sequences, sometimes, it is important to know the imagination as well.
व्याकरण and प्रातिशाख्य deal with this imagination

PART_2_DEFINITION_OF_SANDHI.title: Definition of Sandhi
PART_2_DEFINITION_OF_SANDHI.definition_simple: Sandhi means junction or connection or combination
PART_2_DEFINITION_OF_SANDHI.definition_detailed: When two or more entities meet at a single point, that point can generally be referred to as a 'Sandhi'
PART_2_DEFINITION_OF_SANDHI.linguistic_context: In the context of व्याकरण, those two entities are वर्णs (letters)
PART_2_DEFINITION_OF_SANDHI.important_note: The term 'Sandhi' is used only when two or more वर्णs join or confront 'the results', rather than referring to individual वर्णs
PART_2_DEFINITION_OF_SANDHI.principle: In all sandhis, the first part's last letter and the second part's first letter will be involved
PART_2_DEFINITION_OF_SANDHI.definition_sloka: विशिष्टास्तु स्वराः यत्र व्यञ्जनं वापि योगतः। सन्धीयते पदे यस्मात्तस्मात् सन्धिः प्रकीर्तितः।। इति।

PART_3_SANDHI_RESULT_TYPES.title: Two Main Types of Sandhi Results

TYPE_1_AGAMA.name: आगमसन्धि
TYPE_1_AGAMA.definition: When two or more वर्णs join, a new वर्ण is added to or pronounced along with one of the existing वर्णs

example.explanation: The णकार is added before the ईकार

TYPE_2_ADESHA.name: आदेशसन्धि
TYPE_2_ADESHA.definition: When two or more वर्णs join, a new वर्ण is pronounced in the place of the existing वर्ण

SUBTYPE_1.name: एकादेशसन्धि
SUBTYPE_1.definition: One वर्ण will be replaced in place of two वर्णs

example.explanation: One वर्ण (आकार) replaces the place of अकार and आकार

SUBTYPE_2.name: लोपसन्धि
SUBTYPE_2.definition: One वर्ण will be deleted or omitted or elided

example.explanation: One विसर्ग got omitted, and the other गकार remains the same

PART_3_SANDHI_RESULT_TYPES.IMPORTANT_NOTE: Continuous articulation is NOT sandhi. There must be one of the mentioned actions. Therefore, 'वनम् अत्र' has no sandhi.

PART_4_VARNA_CLASSIFICATION.title: Classification of Varnas
PART_4_VARNA_CLASSIFICATION.definition: The air released from oral parts of human body is shaped into sounds. The smallest sound particle capable of changing meaning is called वर्ण

two_main_types.name: स्वरs
two_main_types.definition: Sound particles not obstructed by any part of mouth
two_main_types.note: Long vowels (दीर्घ) and very long vowels (प्लुत) also included

two_main_types.name: व्यञ्जनs
two_main_types.definition: Sound particles hit or obstructed by any part of mouth

two_main_types.name: उभयाक्षरs / अयोगवाहs
two_main_types.definition: Sometimes not changing meaning, still referred to as 'वर्णs' for grammatical purposes

माहेश्वरसूत्रs.title: 14 Coding Sutras
माहेश्वरसूत्रs.purpose: All स्वर and व्यञ्जन technically coded and listed for maintaining brevity (लाघवम्)

sutras.meaning: Vowels a, i, u + anchor न्
h, y, v, r + anchor ट्
Sibilants: sh, ṣ, s + anchor र्

माहेश्वरसूत्रs.mechanism: Last letter of each sutra acts as anchor to connect with first letter of next sutra

example_अच्.composition: अ, इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ, ए, ओ, ऐ, औ
example_अच्.note: Long vowels (दीर्घ) and very long vowels (प्लुत) also included

PART_5_INTERNAL_VS_EXTERNAL_SANDHI.title: Internal vs External Sandhi

three_analysis_layers.name: द्वितीयः स्तरः
three_analysis_layers.note: Internal sandhis MANDATORY at this level

three_analysis_layers.name: तृतीयः स्तरः
three_analysis_layers.description: Breaking into ultimate roots (धातु) and derivation markers
three_analysis_layers.note: Internal sandhis MANDATORY at this level

internal_sandhi_detailed.definition: Sandhi within a पद (word/unit) - occurs in 2nd and 3rd layers
internal_sandhi_detailed.characteristic: The पद is the full chunk, so last letter is NOT पदान्त

examples.explanation: पद is full chunk 'नायकः', so last letter of 'नै' is not पदान्त
पद is full chunk 'भवति', so last letter of 'भो' is not पदान्त
पद is full chunk 'दैत्यारि', so last letter of 'दैत्य' is not पदान्त

external_sandhi_detailed.definition: Sandhi between different पदs - occurs in 1st layer
external_sandhi_detailed.condition: If speed speech exists, all sandhis should be formed
external_sandhi_detailed.characteristic: वर्णs involved typically part of पद-suffix (सुप् or तिङ्) or related

examples.explanation: वर्ण 'इ' is part of suffix तिङ्, so external and optional
वर्ण 'अ' closely related to सुप्, so external and optional

critical_notes: All internal sandhis are generally mandatory, unless there is an exception
If three वर्णs are involved, the sandhi is external only

PART_6_IMPORTANT_QUESTIONS.title: Three Important Questions for Sandhi Analysis
PART_6_IMPORTANT_QUESTIONS.note: Understanding these three questions helps comprehend all sandhis easily

PART_7_SVARA_SANDHI_COMPREHENSIVE.title: स्वरसन्धि (Vowel Sandhi) - COMPREHENSIVE
PART_7_SVARA_SANDHI_COMPREHENSIVE.general_rule: When two स्वर (vowels) join, they may be joined, replaced, or deleted
PART_7_SVARA_SANDHI_COMPREHENSIVE.characteristic: Most स्वरसन्धिs are only आदेशसन्धिs (substitution type)

RULE_1_YANADESH.name: यणादेशसन्धि
RULE_1_YANADESH.definition: Letters इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ are replaced with य, व, र, ल when followed by a vowel
RULE_1_YANADESH.explanation: 'इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ' called 'इक्', 'य, व, र, ल' called 'यण्'

RULE_2_AYAVAYAVA.name: अयवायावादेशसन्धि
RULE_2_AYAVAYAVA.definition: ए, ऐ, ओ, औ transform when followed by another vowel
RULE_2_AYAVAYAVA.formal_rule: एज्वर्णेभ्यः अचः परत्वेन भवन्ति तर्हि प्रत्येकम्

RULE_3_GUNA.name: गुणसन्धि
RULE_3_GUNA.definition: When अ is followed by इक्/उक्/ऋक्/ऌक्, intermediate vowels are created

RULE_4_VRIDDHI.name: वृद्धिसन्धि
RULE_4_VRIDDHI.definition: When अ is followed by ए/ओ/ऐ/औ, long vowels are created

RULE_5_SAVARNA_DIRGH.name: सवर्णदीर्घसन्धि
RULE_5_SAVARNA_DIRGH.definition: When same vowels meet, they combine into one long vowel
RULE_5_SAVARNA_DIRGH.pattern: Same vowel + Same vowel = One long vowel

RULE_6_PURVARDPA.name: पूर्वरूपसन्धि
RULE_6_PURVARDPA.definition: ए-ओ followed by short अकार - the second vowel is absorbed into the first
RULE_6_PURVARDPA.note: अवग्रहः (ऽ) written to indicate this sandhi. When double ऽऽ appears, दीर्घ आकार forms

EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.rule: If first part ends in ई with dual form, and second starts with अज्, NO sandhi
EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.example: हरी एतौ - here ई doesn't undergo yanadesh

EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.rule: If the last vowel of first part is marked as प्लुत (with 3 dots), NO sandhi
EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.example: राम(3) अत्र, राम(3) इह, राम(3) एहि - no sandhi applied

EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.rule: If first part is एकाज् निपात (indeclinable), NO sandhi
EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.example: इ इन्द्रः, उ उमेशः - no दीर्घसन्धि

EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.rule: If first part is ओ-ending निपात, NO sandhi
If related to अदस् (demonstrative), NO sandhi
EXCEPTIONS_TO_SVARA_SANDHI.example: अमी ईशाः, अमू इमौ - no sandhi

PART_8_VYANJANA_SANDHI.title: व्यञ्जनसन्धि (Consonant Sandhi)
PART_8_VYANJANA_SANDHI.note: There are 33 consonants. Multiple transformations occur based on pratyaharas and place of articulation
PART_8_VYANJANA_SANDHI.key_question: कः भवति?, कदा भवति?, कस्य भवति? - Three questions to understand all व्यञ्जनसन्धिs

PRATYAHARAS.चर्: First consonants of groups (कचटतप) and sibilants (शषस)
PRATYAHARAS.खर्: First two consonants of groups and sibilants
PRATYAHARAS.झश्: Third and fourth consonants of groups
PRATYAHARAS.झय्: First, second, third, fourth consonants of groups
PRATYAHARAS.झल्: All consonants except fifth consonant of groups and semi-vowels
PRATYAHARAS.अट्: All vowels and semi-vowels (य, र, ल, व)

RULE_1_JASHTTVA.name: जश्त्वसन्धि
RULE_1_JASHTTVA.rule: Final झल् consonants become third consonant of their group before झश् consonants
RULE_1_JASHTTVA.when: At पदान्त, when followed by झश्-consonants

RULE_3_SHCHUTVA.name: श्चुत्वसन्धि
RULE_3_SHCHUTVA.rule: स् + तवर्ग → श् + चवर्ग before च्छ्ज्झ्ञ्

RULE_4_SHTUTVA.name: ष्टुत्वसन्धि
RULE_4_SHTUTVA.rule: स् + तवर्ग → ष् + टवर्ग before ट्ठ्ड्ढ्

RULE_6_ANUSVARA.name: अनुस्वारसन्धि
RULE_6_ANUSVARA.note: अनुस्वार alone doesn't satisfy phonetic requirements - parasavarna necessary

RULE_7_ANUSVARA_PARASAVARNA.name: अनुस्वारपरसवर्णसन्धि
RULE_7_ANUSVARA_PARASAVARNA.yay_includes: Velar group, Palatal group, Retroflex group, Dental group, Labial group, Semi-vowels

RULE_8_LAKARA_PARASAVARNA.name: लकारपरसवर्णसन्धि
RULE_8_LAKARA_PARASAVARNA.note: Sanskrit doesn't allow ल् + non-ल् consonants

RULE_9_TUGAGAMA.name: तुगागमसन्धि
RULE_9_TUGAGAMA.rule: Short vowel + छ् → तुग् added before छ्

external_examples.before: पूर्वपदे दीर्घ हो तो तुगागमः विकल्पेन भवति

RULE_10_PURVASA VARNA_ADESHA.name: पूर्वसवर्णादेशसन्धि
RULE_10_PURVASA VARNA_ADESHA.rule: पदान्त झय्-consonants + ह् → homorganic consonant + ह्

PART_9_THREE_VARNA_SANDHI.title: वर्णत्रयापेक्षितसन्धयः (Three-Varna Sandhi)
PART_9_THREE_VARNA_SANDHI.definition: Sandhis where three वर्णs are involved

RULE_2_NGMUDAGAMA.name: ङमुडागमसन्धि
RULE_2_NGMUDAGAMA.rule: Nasal addition based on preceding consonant's group

PART_10_VISARGA_SANDHI_EXPANDED.title: विसर्गसन्धि - COMPREHENSIVE WITH ALL EXAMPLES
PART_10_VISARGA_SANDHI_EXPANDED.definition: विसर्गः undergoes multiple transformations based on context

TYPE_1_VISARGA_LOPA.name: 1. विसर्गलोपः
TYPE_1_VISARGA_LOPA.condition: अकारान्तः + : + उत्तरपदे अ भिन्नस्वरः = विसर्ग is deleted

TYPE_2_OGUNA.name: 2. ओकारत्वेन (when अ: + अ)
TYPE_2_OGUNA.rule: अ: + अ → अ + ऽ (with अवग्रहः) or अ: + ओ + अ

TYPE_3_OGUNA_HAV_RAV.name: 3. विसर्गः ओकारत्वम् (अ: + ह्, य्, व्, र्)

TYPE_4_RAKARA.name: 4. रकारादेशः (विसर्ग: becomes र् before non-अ vowel)

TYPE_5_NO_CHANGE.name: 5. क्, ख्, प्, फ् - NO SANDHI
TYPE_5_NO_CHANGE.rule: Visarga before these consonants remains unchanged

PART_11_INTERACTION_AND_PRECEDENCE.title: Sandhi Interaction Rules & Stage-by-Stage Analysis
PART_11_INTERACTION_AND_PRECEDENCE.principle: Multiple stages may apply before final form
PART_11_INTERACTION_AND_PRECEDENCE.critical: Must check PREVIOUS transformations before applying new rules

EXAMPLE_1.note: NO गुणसन्धि at stage 3, even though अ + इ could form ए

EXAMPLE_2.note: NO दीर्घसन्धि even though अ + अ could form आ

key_principles: Three questions essential: कः भवति?, कदा भवति?, कस्य भवति?
Multiple simultaneous transformations can affect rules
FINAL_SUMMARY.note: These are the very important sandhis. Many other sandhis follow typical system and logic.
